column1: # Game profile of Pokémon Sword (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.3.2 = v458752, both DLC licences). In bring-up (docs/stageA-sword-bringup.md)
# Game Freak's engine, SDK 7.3.2, NVN 7.3.2, NintendoWare Font / Ui2d / Vfx / G3d, Wwise audio; modules main + subsdk0 (NintendoSDK_movie) + subsdk1 (GLSLC) + sdk.
# RomFS: 50,494 files, 12.1 GB; almost every model, texture and shader sits in GFLXPACK archives (.gfpak, raw / zlib / LZ4 entries), 577 loose BNSH files.
# Started from the survey's provisional profile; every value below was checked on the Mac (first-boot language select, naming, opening scene in Postwick)
# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID

# Silicon Studio's YEBIS 3 (bloom, glare, tone map, final composite) keeps its 3,155 GLSLC outputs in one TinyEffect object (".tfxo file", 39.5 MB) compressed as a 3.2 MB zlib stream in main's read-only segment;
# shader_split.py inflates it (zlib_streams): 3,015 more keys in the tables, 46 of them used on the route to Postwick
# every module main imports from (subsdk1 is GLSLC; the game compiles no GLSL at run time on the routes tried, DM_GLSLC_CAPTURE stayed empty)

# The NPDM declares no system resource: main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB (3.13 GB measured), inside a 3.25 GB heap region of a 4 GB reservation (under iOS's 6 GB limit without extended VA)
# the rewritten modules are larger than the default 64 MB of used memory the game takes off the pool for its heap
# one group per RomFS area, so a rebuild after a change in one area keeps the others' libraries
